fault_line: An act of war demanding a NATO response -- or an intel claim without public evidence?

sections.what_happened: WSJ reported Oct 20 that US intelligence agencies assess the failed early-August drone attack on Leipzig-Halle Airport -- explosive-packed drones aimed at an Antonov freighter used to carry military aid to Ukraine; one drone hit the freighter but failed to explode, another collided with a different plane, a third detonated near the airport perimeter -- was one of the opening shots in a stepped-up campaign of sabotage and covert action against NATO countries ordered directly by Russian President Vladimir Putin, according to European officials briefed on US intel findings. German officials say the drones were piloted by Russian military-intelligence agents. Context: Tagesschau reported an explosive drone found at Leipzig/Halle on Aug 5; DW carried footage Aug 7. The WSJ story was missed by all scans Oct 20-24 (zero prior 'sabotage' records).
sections.what_verified: WSJ (T2) as originator; Meduza (T2) relays the WSJ findings -- a distinct publisher family but NOT independent confirmation of the assessment. Tagesschau/DW confirm only the August Leipzig drone incident, not the Putin-order claim.
sections.what_disputed: No public evidence has been published tying Putin's order to Leipzig; German commentators (3.7K likes/640 comments reel) openly ask why no NATO Article 4 consultation was requested and why no Article 5 case was pursued if the threat is as stated; no Russian response was located in this scan (gap, not a denial). The underlying Leipzig incident is attributed by German officials to Russian military-intelligence agents per WSJ -- itself an attribution, not a court finding.
sections.why_matters: A drone attack on a German cargo airport in August -- now US intel says Putin ordered it personally. The evidence is still classified; the argument is already public.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (big-missed; WSJ Oct 20) -- US intel assesses Putin personally ordered a stepped-up NATO sabotage campaign; Leipzig airport drone attack was an opening shot

totw_analysis: Our read: A drone attack on a German cargo airport in August -- now US intel says Putin ordered it personally. The evidence is still classified; the argument is already public. The fault line our audience is arguing over: An act of war demanding a NATO response -- or an intel claim without public evidence?
